stories.title: Street medicine vendors are dangerously filling Haiti’s healthcare gaps
stories.summary: Image by Global Voices, created using Canva elements. Haiti is a country with very few health facilities and a dearth of healthcare workers to meet people’s needs. Public hospitals lack basic medical equipment, demand far exceeds staff capacity, and administrative problems are rife. Other health centres, usually run by non-profit organisations, help some of the most vulnerable people, while private hospitals are few and far between, given that most Haitians cannot afford to pay for treatment there. Even the wealthy are often forced to go abroad for treatment when faced with critical health issues. This already dire situation became worse when gangs from the Viv Ansanm criminal coalition began targeting both public and private health facilities, looting many of them, stealing equipment, and even setting fire to some of the properties. Health centres located in gang-controlled areas are often forced to close temporarily because of fights that break out between rival gangs.

stories.title: Everglades National Park Announces Winter Programs and Special Events
stories.summary: News Release Date: November 17, 2026 Contact: Media contact , 786-897-1053 Contact: Park information , 305-242-7700 HOMESTEAD, Fla. — Everglades National Park has announced its 2026-27 winter season schedule, with expanded visitor center hours and ranger-led programs across all four park districts. Offerings include wildlife watching, wet walks, paddling, stargazing and special events. Some seasonal programs are already underway and the full winter schedule begins Dec. stories.title: Work and Pensions Secretary statement on the Milburn review into young people and work
stories.summary: The Rt Hon Pat McFadden MP, Secretary of State for Work and Pensions, responded to the publication of the independent Milburn review into young people and work. This morning, Alan Milburn published a landmark report, setting out a radical blueprint for a new settlement with young people. Because one million young people not in education, employment or training creates a human cost that no country should ask its young people to bear. It robs them of the thing that is most important to their lives – the prospect of a good future.

facts.text: Work and Pensions Secretary statement on the Milburn review into young people and work
The Rt Hon Pat McFadden MP, Secretary of State for Work and Pensions, responded to the publication of the independent Milburn review into young people and work.
With your permission, Mr Speaker, I would like to make a statement on the Milburn review into young people and work.
This morning, Alan Milburn published a landmark report, setting out a radical blueprint for a new settlement with young people.
I want to thank Mr Milburn and his team for their outstanding work.
Sometimes a review deals with an issue so fundamental that it alters what we see as the contract between Government and society.
Because one million young people not in education, employment or training creates a human cost that no country should ask its young people to bear.
It robs them of the thing that is most important to their lives – the prospect of a good future.

stories.title: UK leads international cooperation on sustainable export finance
stories.summary: New international report shows $376 billion in export finance is now covered by net-zero commitments, up 58% in a year. The report was published as governments and businesses gather for COP31. NZECA is chaired by UK Export Finance (UKEF), the UK’s export credit agency. Its new report shows that the value of members’ export finance covered by net-zero commitments has risen from $238 billion to $376 billion. These commitments aim to reduce the emissions linked to this finance over time. The UK has chaired NZECA since the network was launched at COP28 in 2023. The alliance was convened by the UN Environment Programme Finance Initiative to help export credit agencies and export-import banks reach net-zero by 2050. Its membership includes Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Kazakhstan, Spain, Sweden, the United Arab Emirates and the UK. Export credit agencies and export-import banks are government-backed bodies that help businesses sell goods and services overseas.

on_this_day.title: The Suez Canal opens
on_this_day.summary: The Suez Canal officially opened on 17 November 1869. Located in Egypt, it connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea. Ships using the canal can travel between these seas without sailing around southern Africa. The opening was a significant moment in the history of maritime transport. The canal also has a complex political history, showing how a piece of infrastructure can matter to both travel and international affairs.
